citations.narrative:
The facility is conducting regulated activity without a license from USDA APHIS Animal Care under the Animal Welfare
Act (AWA). An inventory from a licensed pet store shows this individual has sold approximately 64 hamsters, 100 guinea
pigs, 50 gerbils, and 5 rabbits to the licensee between December 2024 and September 2025. When contacted, the
licensee admitted selling hamsters, guinea pigs, gerbils, and rabbits to the licensee. She stated she had ten gerbils last
year, but doesn't know how many were female. She also admitted to having 5 female hamsters, 3 female rabbits, and 30
guinea total pigs last year. A search was previously conducted on this individual on 2/19/17. The facility representative
was made aware of what is and isn't regulated activity at that time. An application packet was also sent out to the facility
representative.
Conducting regulated activity without a USDA license does not allow for the inspection of the regulated animals' health
and well-being in accordance with the Animal Welfare Act. Continuing to conduct regulated activity without a license is a
serious violation of the Animal Welfare Act. The customer must either stop conducting regulated activity or the customer
must obtain a USDA license.
NO REGULATED ACTIVITIES MAY BE CONDUCTED UNTIL A LICENSE IS OBTAINED.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
